overview: Alectrosaurus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid from Late Cretaceous Asia. PBDB records a broad Central Asian distribution including Inner Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, with formations such as Iren Dabasu, Bissekty, Khodzhakul and Bostobe.

Its importance lies in the pre-Tyrannosaurus phase of tyrannosauroid history: Alectrosaurus documents a more gracile, geographically widespread Asian predator before the deepest-skulled tyrannosaurids dominated latest Cretaceous ecosystems.

fossilSites.name: Iren Dabasu Formation
fossilSites.note: One of several PBDB-listed formations for Alectrosaurus-like tyrannosauroid material.

fossilSites.name: Bissekty and Khodzhakul formations
fossilSites.note: Central Asian records contributing to the broad PBDB range for the taxon.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: Alectrosaurus helps bridge the gap between early tyrannosauroids and the later giant tyrannosaurids of Asia and North America.

articles.title: Evidence limit
articles.body: The PBDB occurrence spread is broad, so some referred material may need taxonomic review rather than being treated as equally secure.

record.description: Alectrosaurus olseni was a medium-sized tyrannosauroid from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia. The name is anchored by an associated hind limb; much cranial and forelimb material once assigned to it belongs to other theropods.
facts: The secure type material is chiefly a partial hind limb and foot.
Recent work supports tyrannosauroid affinities but cannot recover a complete body from the limited diagnostic material.

review.ageReviewNote: The Iren Dabasu Formation has a debated, broad Late Cretaceous age, probably within the Cenomanian-Campanian interval.

evidence.material: An associated partial hind limb and limited referred remains.
evidence.confidenceLimit: Sparse diagnostic material prevents precise size, skull and ecology claims.
uncertainties: Historical cranial and forelimb referrals are excluded.
Its exact tyrannosauroid position is unresolved.
